title: 2026-07-21 Redwood discovery with Mariner Logistics
summary: Discovery focused on unit economics for inference. Mariner runs a multi-tenant customer support summarization pipeline with variable prompt lengths and bursty traffic. Discussion covered hosted cost vs Dedicated reserved capacity, caching/prefix reuse, batch sizing, quantization, expected QPS, and security requirements. Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing sheets, run a benchmark with sample prompts, schedule security review, and scope a 30-day dedicated pilot if numbers align.
next_steps: Sofia to send detailed per-token pricing and example cost model by 2026-07-23
Emily to share representative 1k prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-07-24
Schedule security deep-dive (SOC2, SSO, KMS) with Mariner security team week of 2026-07-27
Liam to coordinate pilot infra sizing and estimate for Dedicated trial by 2026-07-26
action_items: Sofia Martinez: email pricing sheet + example cost calculations; due 2026-07-23
Emily Chen: upload 1k sample prompts and latency targets; due 2026-07-24
Liam O'Connor: prepare pilot sizing (GPU type, estimated qps, batch config) and run rough cost calc; due 2026-07-26
Derek Huang: confirm VPC peering and IAM constraints for Private deployment options; due 2026-07-28
transcript:
00:00 Sofia Martinez: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Sofia from Redwood, i'm the AE on this one.
00:05 Liam O'Connor: hey team.
00:08 Rajiv Patel: hi, thanks for doing this, we wanted to focus on cost and how we can keep economics predictable.
00:17 Sofia Martinez: great, yeah we hear that a lot—especially for customer support summarization. can you give us current stack and volumes?
00:26 Emily Chen: sure, we run a mix of short ticket summaries (~30-80 tokens) and longer case summaries (~400-600 tokens). baseline is about 150 qps during peak, but obviously bursts up to 800 qps for 10-15 minutes during outages.
00:44 Liam O'Connor: ok, that's helpful. are you using any prefix caching or reuse today?
00:49 Emily Chen: not really, we're mostly calling a hosted model and do minimal caching at the app layer.
00:55 Derek Huang: infra wise we use AWS, VPCs, standard SAML SSO, and we do KMS for keys. security is a must.
01:05 Sofia Martinez: understood. on the cost side we typically break it down per input token + output token for hosted. for Dedicated we give committed capacity pricing, which usually translates to lower per-token unit economics for sustained throughput.
01:20 Rajiv Patel: can you give an example? ballpark numbers?
01:23 Sofia Martinez: for hosted, depending on model family, you're looking at $0.0008 to $0.003 per 1k input tokens for open LLMs—apologies those brackets vary—and output tokens similar. for a 400-token response you'd compute the input+output. for Dedicated we do a committed monthly GPU pool; effective per-token can drop by 40-60% if you fully utilize the pool.
01:44 Emily Chen: that range is pretty wide; main thing for us is predictability—our CFO wants a budget cap not a surprise line item.
01:52 Liam O'Connor: that's where batching and KV/prefix caching become levers: if you can reuse context or cache common prefixes you save on generation work. also we can recommend quantized model variants that maintain quality but reduce GPU memory and cost.
02:06 Rajiv Patel: curious on batching tradeoffs—i.e., latency impact if we enable larger batch sizes for throughput.
02:12 Liam O'Connor: typically continuous batching trades a bit of tail latency for much higher throughput. with Redwood's runtime you can configure SLO windows and burst lanes: small requests stay low-latency, large requests get queued briefly to form efficient batches. you can also reserve a fraction of capacity for low-latency traffic.
02:28 Derek Huang: do you have metrics for how much batching reduces per-token cost?
02:32 Sofia Martinez: rough rule of thumb: effective token cost can drop 2-3x with aggressive batching and KV cache for repeated prefixes; actual depends on prompt distribution and reuse rates.
02:42 Emily Chen: our reuse rate is low except for canned responses; most are unique.
02:47 Liam O'Connor: then caching helps less, but batching still helps for throughput. another lever is prefix KV cache for conversation-style flows—saves both compute and latency.
02:57 Rajiv Patel: what's the pilot flow if we wanted to validate numbers?
03:01 Sofia Martinez: we typically do a 30-day Dedicated pilot: we size a GPU pool to your peak-ish load, run your representative prompt set, and you pay a reduced pilot fee. we run benchmarking, show latency/cost curves, and then you can choose hosted, Dedicated commit, or Private.
03:15 Emily Chen: does the pilot require giving you data? data residency is a concern.
03:19 Sofia Martinez: for Dedicated pilots we can do VPC peering or a Private deployment option; you keep keys in KMS and control network access. we also support bringing your own key material (HSM integration) for Private.
03:32 Derek Huang: ok that's good. timeline for Dedicated commit—how long to ramp?
03:36 Liam O'Connor: initial provisioning typically 1-2 weeks for Dedicated pools if capacity's available; Private on-prem is longer.
03:42 Rajiv Patel: sample calculation—say average response 400 tokens, 150 qps baseline. what does that look like per month?
03:49 Sofia Martinez: quick calc: 400 tokens * 150 qps * 3600 sec * 24 hours * 30 days is huge, but you're not running 24/7 at peak. better to convert to monthly active average. if average utilization equals 20% of peak sustained, the monthly token count is much lower. we offered to run a modeled sheet—we'll need your real traffic histogram.
04:10 Emily Chen: we'll share a week's histogram, that should help.
04:14 Rajiv Patel: also our budget: CFO mentioned $25k/month for inference. can we get within that?
04:20 Liam O'Connor: depends on choices—hosted will be pricier at scale but lower operational overhead. Dedicated with good utilization can get you under $25k/mo; Private has higher fixed infra and engineering costs.
04:33 Sofia Martinez: also feature tradeoffs: hosted gives fastest time-to-value and Redwood handles scaling, patching, variance in models. Dedicated gives cost predictability and isolation. Private gives max control and compliance but you manage infra.
04:47 Derek Huang: regarding compliance: you mentioned SOC2, SSO, and audit logs—can you give docs?
04:52 Sofia Martinez: yes we'll send SOC2 report excerpt, SSO/SAML setup guide, and KMS/HSM integration docs as part of the security packet.
04:59 Emily Chen: on model variants—do you recommend off-the-shelf open models or Redwood-curated variants?
05:04 Liam O'Connor: for cost-sensitive workloads we often recommend smaller quantized variants with evaluation against your prompts—sometimes a 7B quantized model gives acceptable quality at a fraction of the cost vs 13B/70B. Redwood Optimize also suggests quant profiles per workload.
05:19 Rajiv Patel: what's the rollback story if quality drops after switching models?
05:23 Sofia Martinez: we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies; you can run A/B tests and automatic fallback to ensure production stability.
05:31 Emily Chen: network-wise, for Private we need peering and strict IP allowlisting—Derek is going to validate.
05:36 Derek Huang: yes we'll check firewall and procurement for on-prem if needed.
05:40 Rajiv Patel: any hidden fees e.g. egress or storage?
05:44 Sofia Martinez: hosted has egress considerations for embeddings export, but for inference tokens that's included. Dedicated contracts include data retention charges if you want long-term logs beyond default retention; we'll list those in the pricing sheet.
05:58 Liam O'Connor: for benchmarking we'll run the prompt set with representative concurrency patterns—we'll show cost per effective request for hosted vs Dedicated with a utilization curve.
06:08 Emily Chen: can you also show us break-even points—at what sustained qps Dedicated becomes cheaper?
06:12 Sofia Martinez: yes, that's standard; we'll model per-token costs vs utilization and show the crossover point.
06:18 Rajiv Patel: ok this is helpful. next steps recap?
06:21 Sofia Martinez: we'll send pricing and security docs, Liam will size pilot, Emily will hand over prompts, Derek will check network/security constraints, and we'll reconvene after we have the benchmark results.
06:32 Rajiv Patel: thanks, looking forward to the pilot.
06:35 Sofia Martinez: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with timelines and sheet.
06:38 [call ends]
